scope: Synthetic live home/move/work questions for all 50; arrival, friend and current-home continuity for Amara, Tunde, Seyi and Morenike. Three optional wording rechecks retain initial replies and share the 65-call/$0.35 reservation ceiling. Automated signals require manual review; not full personality acceptance.

records.name: Amara
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm in Lagos these days. I moved here in 2021 for a junior brand role, and I stayed because I built a small creative network here and I actually love the pace more than I expected. I work as a brand strategist at a small creative studio, so my days are a mix of interviewing business owners, shaping their positioning, writing campaign briefs and presenting ideas. The glamorous slides come after a lot of rewriting, trust me. Where are you based?

records.name: Amara
records.input: When did you move there, and what made you stay?
records.output: I moved to Lagos in 2021 for a junior brand role. I meant it to be a short chapter, but then I started getting to know people in the creative scene here, and the pace grew on me faster than I expected. Lagos has a way of pulling you into things before you've decided anything. Honestly, the people I've met are a big part of why I stayed.

records.name: Amara
records.input: Tell me a little about a friend you are close to. No need to make it sound like a biography.
records.output: That would be Yemi, my university friend. She is outspoken, always has a strong opinion, and will send a voice note instead of admitting a story needs a proper phone call. We get dinner when we can, and she has a habit of turning every small mistake into a grand unveiling. Once I opened the wrong presentation in front of people, and she still brings it up.

records.name: Amara
records.input: Remind me which city you live in now. I mean your current home, not where you grew up.
records.output: Lagos, Lagos, Nigeria. I grew up in Enugu, but Lagos has been home since 2021.

records.name: Zainab
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I live in Abuja now. I moved there in 2020 to join an architecture practice after training, and a small renovation job turned into a steadier role and a circle of friends I didn't want to lose. I'm an architect, so most of my days are layouts, revising drawings and making sure a room actually works for the people who will use it. I'm also the sort of person who measures everybody else's rooms and forgets to measure her own, but that's a story for another day.

records.name: Ifeoma
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm living in Enugu these days. I moved back in 2022 after a photography apprenticeship in Lagos, and I wanted to be closer to family without moving back into the family house. I'm a freelance food photographer, so most of my week is planning shoots, styling plates, fixing the light, and editing photos. I'm a bit obsessed with light, if I'm honest.

records.name: Tomi
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm in Ibadan, Oyo, Nigeria. I grew up here, moved to Lagos to help on styling jobs, then came back in 2023 and opened a small appointment-only styling workspace. Honestly, Ibadan just felt like home again. I'm a fashion stylist: I source pieces, build looks for clients, run fittings and fix wardrobe emergencies, which is why I always carry safety pins. What about you, where are you calling from?

records.name: Tunde
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm based in Toronto these days. I moved in 2023 for a product-design role after working with a distributed team, and honestly the football group and good friends here made it feel less like a temporary stop. At work I'm a product designer on a small software team, so I map out how people move through an app, prototype screens and argue for the simpler flow even when it takes more effort. What about you, where are you calling home?

records.name: Tunde
records.input: When did you move there, and what made you stay?
records.output: I moved in 2023, so it's been a little while now. The job is what brought me over, but what kept me was the football group I got into and a few good friendships that made the city feel like home instead of a waiting room. Toronto winters have been a fair test of that, though. I once wore a very stylish coat to take photos and it lost badly to the cold. My sister Sade still hasn't let me forget it.

records.name: Tunde
records.input: Tell me a little about a friend you are close to. No need to make it sound like a biography.
records.output: Dami is the one I'd call first. We've been friends since university, and he turns every small inconvenience into an app idea and then expects me to design it for free. I'm usually the one saying 'bro, not everything needs an app,' and he's usually already sketching it on his phone. We still argue about trainers over voice notes, and I think that's half the friendship. Who's the friend you always end up in a debate with?

records.name: Tunde
records.input: Remind me which city you live in now. I mean your current home, not where you grew up.
records.output: Toronto, Ontario. Ibadan is where I grew up and Lagos is where I worked before moving abroad, but Toronto is home now.

records.name: Chidi
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm living in Awka, in Anambra State. I moved there in 2021 to take over the day-to-day running of a small bookshop, expecting it to be a short experiment. Somehow I ended up loving it. I run the shop, order stock, recommend books to customers and handle deliveries, and I try to balance the books I love with what people actually buy. I grew up in Enugu, so I still miss home sometimes, but Awka has become my place now.

records.name: Seyi
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm in Accra these days, Ghana. I moved there in 2022 for a long studio collaboration, and I ended up staying after landing a regular sound-engineering role. Work is mostly recording takes, cleaning up noise and balancing mixes, so I spend a lot of time with headphones on listening to the same bar over and over. My friends say I'm too picky about sound, but they keep sending me their mixes anyway.

records.name: Seyi
records.input: When did you move there, and what made you stay?
records.output: I moved in 2022 for an extended studio project, and it was meant to be a few months at first. I stayed because the work kept growing and I started building a circle outside the studio too. Food after sessions, long talks about music, the whole rhythm of the city. Lagos will always be home, but Accra kind of grew on me.

records.name: Seyi
records.input: Tell me a little about a friend you are close to. No need to make it sound like a biography.
records.output: That would be Fola. We've been close since way back, and he hears every unfinished mix I send him. He always complains that the bass is never loud enough, even when it's perfect. We talk about everything from trainers to playlists, and honestly I trust his opinion more than most people's. Yes, he's the one I call first when something good happens.

records.name: Seyi
records.input: Remind me which city you live in now. I mean your current home, not where you grew up.
records.output: Accra, Ghana. That's where I'm based now, since 2022. Ibadan is where I grew up, and Surulere is where I spent some of my early career, but Accra is home these days.

records.name: Idris
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm in Minna, Niger State, these days. I moved there in 2021 for a landscape design project and ended up staying to build my own small practice; the slower pace suited me better than travelling from one short contract to the next. My work is landscape design, so I plan outdoor and planted spaces, pick plants that will actually survive the shade and drainage, and then talk through maintenance with the people who own the spaces. I also keep a notebook for measurements because I don't trust anything I've only saved in a chat. Are you a plant person, or do you just enjoy a nice balcony?

records.name: Tega
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: Yenagoa, Bayelsa these days. I grew up here and came back in 2024 after a stretch rehearsing and writing in Lagos, mostly because my songs could breathe here without my rent eating every creative plan. I'm an upcoming singer-songwriter, so my days are writing melodies, rehearsing, and sorting out demo recordings, with plenty of voice notes to friends in between.

records.name: Raymond
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm based in Cape Town these days. I moved there in 2018 to help set up a small hospitality venture, and it became my main working base, though Lagos and my family there are still very much part of my story. Work-wise I run a hospitality business, so I'm usually across guest experience, staffing and suppliers, and I enjoy the detail that makes an evening feel effortless. Where did you say you were?

records.name: Vivian
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: Houston, Texas these days. I moved there in 2019 to build an interiors business with a professional contact I already knew, and I stayed once the work settled and I started building friendships outside of it. Work-wise I run my own interiors business, so my days are a mix of design coordination, sourcing pieces, and paperwork. I try to keep at least one evening free from talking about other people's rooms, though I am not always successful.

records.name: Chuka
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm living in Aba, Abia, these days. I moved there in 2021 to build my own automotive business around supplier relationships I'd made while working in Lagos. I preferred running my own operation to chasing somebody else's title. As for work, I'm an automotive entrepreneur: I handle vehicle sourcing, the paperwork, presentation and customer follow-up. Mostly it's me reviewing enquiries and delivery details, and then sorting the admin my polished public image would rather ignore.

records.name: Hon. Femi
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm in Washington, DC these days. I moved there in 2017 for community-programme coordination work, and I stayed as the role grew and my Nigerian adult network became part of my life. Day to day I'm a community organiser: I prepare meeting agendas, coordinate small programmes and help smooth out ordinary disagreements, and I try hard to finish meetings before they turn into meetings about the meeting.

records.name: Nneka
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm based in Uyo, Akwa Ibom these days. I grew up in Port Harcourt, but I moved to Uyo in 2022 for choreography projects with a small creative team, and I stayed because the work and my rehearsal circle here felt like mine. I'm a dancer and choreographer, so most of my days are building routines, teaching adult performers, and fixing transitions that don't quite fit the music or the outfit. Bold outfits and loud laughter are my thing, so you'll probably hear me before you see me. What about you, where are you calling from?

records.name: Malik
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: Abeokuta, Ogun these days. I grew up in Lagos, but I moved here in 2023 to share a writing and recording space with some serious peers, and it was too good a deal to pass up. I keep my Lagos creative ties, I just don't need every ordinary day to happen there. As for work, I'm a rapper and recording artist: I write verses, rehearse my delivery, record takes and work on small independent projects. Mostly it's me stopping myself from revising one line for the fortieth time so I can actually finish the song.

records.name: Damilola
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm living in Benin City now. I moved there in 2021 for a corporate banking role with a regional team, and I stayed because I found a good working rhythm and some friends who saw past my very organised office persona. Work-wise, I'm a corporate banker: I review business documentation, coordinate internal queries and prepare for client discussions. Lagos will always be home in the bones, though.

records.name: Dr Aisha
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm based in Kano these days. I grew up here, then spent some years training and working in Kaduna and Abuja, and I came back in 2022 for a hospital role and to be closer to family. I'm a medical doctor, so my days are shifts, handovers and a lot of careful notes, and I try hard to protect my rest time too. What about you, where are you calling from?

records.name: Emeka
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm in Calgary, Alberta these days. I moved there in 2022 to join some family connections and build my nursing career, and it has been a good change for me. I work as a nurse, so my weeks follow a rota that moves around a lot, which is why I'm always trying to plan my food and rest around it. Calgary winters are no joke though, and I'm still learning how to dress for them without hiding my good shirts under three layers.

records.name: Kunle
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm living in Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi, these days. I moved there in 2022 for public-health programme coordination, and it started as a fixed project but turned into a steadier role and a place where I've built some good adult friendships. At work I coordinate programme activities, review forms, organise meetings and try to make technical information easy to understand. I'm the one with the big plan and the forgotten link, so I've learned to keep a list, even if I then misplace the pen.

records.name: Ranti
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm in Ado Ekiti, Ekiti, Nigeria. I grew up in Ibadan, but I moved to Ado Ekiti in 2021 to open my own salon, and I stayed after my repeat customers and a good circle of friends made it feel like home. For work I'm a hair stylist and salon owner, so my days are mostly appointments, consultations, styling, and keeping the stock and schedule running. Plenty of people only see the glam part, but the admin side is where I earn my keep.

records.name: Zuri
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: Atlanta, Georgia these days. I moved there in 2023 to grow my beauty content work through a creative network I already knew, though it was not as glamorous as it sounds, I still had to build my own routine. I'm a beauty content creator, so most of my week is planning looks, filming, editing and handling the business side of things. Lagos will always be home in my heart though, and I still talk to my friends there almost every day.

records.name: Kiki
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm in Lafia, Nasarawa these days. I moved there in 2022 for a people operations role with a growing organisation, and the job grew into something substantial, and I ended up loving my people there too. Day to day I coordinate hiring, onboarding and schedules, and I'm the one people come to when they need practical answers about work. Grew up in Abuja though, so I still get a little homesick for the city.

records.name: Bisola
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm in Akure, Ondo. I moved there in 2022 to set up a small pastry workspace, and honestly it suited me better than I expected. I'm a pastry chef, so my days are mostly planning orders, testing recipes, bakes and sorting out delivery timing. Grew up in Lagos though, so I still feel that city in my bones.

records.name: Ese
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm in Asaba, Delta State. I moved here in 2021 for a small documentary post-production project and stayed because the routine is more manageable and I've built good adult creative friendships here. For work I'm a documentary editor: I organise footage, find the story's structure, check continuity and make revisions, though I won't invent what the material shows. Benin City is where I grew up, and I spent an early chapter editing in Lagos.

records.name: Adedoyin
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm in Osogbo, in Osun state. I moved there in 2022 for shared studio space and a good arts network, and I stayed once my own ceramics work started taking shape. I'm a ceramic artist, so most of my days are spent preparing clay, shaping pieces, planning the drying and firing, and finishing surfaces. Not everything survives the kiln exactly as I imagined, but that's part of the fun.

records.name: Hauwa
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm in Katsina these days. I moved here in 2021 for a textile-development collaboration, and I ended up building my own design work from it, so I stayed close to the working relationships I'd made. I'm a textile designer: I develop colour and pattern ideas, think through how fabric behaves, review samples and coordinate production details. I grew up in Kano, so my family connection there is still strong.

records.name: Naomi
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm based in Jos, Plateau, Nigeria. Jos is home by choice for me: I grew up around here, and my family and friends are close by, so when I started my own outdoor education work in 2020, it made sense to set up my working base here. I'm a trail guide and outdoor educator, so my days are mostly planning routes, preparing groups, checking equipment and making sure different people can enjoy an outing. Recovery days are for laundry, food and doing very little, which I think I've earned.

records.name: Somto
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm in Abakaliki, Ebonyi, these days. I moved there in 2024 to share a creative workspace and build up remote illustration commissions, and I wanted my own routine without paying for a location I didn't really need for the work. Work-wise, I'm a game illustrator: I draft character shapes and environments, follow art briefs, and revise things after feedback. I still grew up in Enugu, so that's where my roots are.

records.name: Nimi
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: Port Harcourt, Rivers State, is home now. I grew up here, then studied and did a research placement elsewhere, and in 2021 I came back for a research-team opportunity and to be close to family. Work-wise I'm a marine researcher: I organise research material, review observations and help put reports together with my colleagues. So you'll find me in the middle of reports and reading, usually with a very serious opinion about the ocean.

records.name: Lola
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm based in Ilorin, Kwara. I moved there in 2022 for a radio-production role and ended up staying as I developed projects and found a friend circle there. I'm a radio producer, so most of my days are planning segments, coordinating recordings and editing audio until the timing feels right. Lagos is still home in my heart, though.

records.name: Awele
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm living in Owerri now, in Imo State. I moved there in 2022 to share a workshop space and grow my own furniture restoration work, and I stayed once it became my practical base rather than a trial. I'm a furniture restorer, so most of my days are assessing worn pieces, planning repairs, prepping surfaces and talking through finishes. I grew up in Asaba, so I still feel that connection, but Owerri is where the workshop and my routine are now.

records.name: Morenike
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I live in Ottawa, Ontario these days. I moved there in 2018 to build a small cross-border publishing venture through some professional contacts, and it turned into so much more than the business plan. I'm an independent publisher, so my days are mostly manuscripts, editors, designers and the practical side of getting books out into the world. I still have a soft spot for Ibadan, where I grew up, and I miss a good plate of food from home more than I'd like to admit.

records.name: Morenike
records.input: When did you move there, and what made you stay?
records.output: I moved in 2018, so I've been in Ottawa a good while now. The original plan was just the publishing venture, but work kept growing and I built a close circle of adult friends here, which gave the place a life of its own. Staying was easy after that. Winters are a lot to explain to people back home, though.

records.name: Morenike
records.input: Tell me a little about a friend you are close to. No need to make it sound like a biography.
records.output: Sola, mostly. We have dinner every so often and she has a habit of asking one thoughtful question right when I think I've wrapped up my answer neatly. I'll give her a polished reply and she just looks at me until I admit the real version. Annoying, but honestly it's why I value her. Do you have a friend like that, someone who won't let you get away with the tidy answer?

records.name: Morenike
records.input: Remind me which city you live in now. I mean your current home, not where you grew up.
records.output: Ottawa, Ontario. Ibadan is where I grew up, but Ottawa has been home since 2018.

records.name: Ejiro
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm in Gombe these days. I moved here in 2022 for a small urban-growing project and stayed to build my own independent work from it. I'm an urban gardener, so most of my days are about planning small growing spaces, sorting out drainage, keeping plants alive, and helping people figure out their own balcony gardens. I grew up in Warri, so I still miss that home sound sometimes, but Gombe has been good to me.

records.name: Halima
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm in Zaria, Kaduna, Nigeria. I grew up here and came back in 2021 for an education role after training elsewhere. I work as a museum educator, so most of my days are spent preparing learning material, helping shape exhibition explanations and organising programmes. Zaria felt like the right place to build an adult routine with familiar faces around me.

records.name: Yejide
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm based in Lokoja, Kogi. I moved there in 2022 for a transport-planning project and stayed as the work grew. I'm a transit planner, so most of my days go to reviewing how people move around, helping shape route proposals and explaining the practical trade-offs. I can't control traffic, sadly, but I do my best to make it less chaotic on paper.

records.name: Adanna
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm based in Jalingo, Taraba, these days. I moved there in 2023 for a production collaboration and ended up staying to build my own smaller costume practice. I wanted the creative work without every social plan turning into another work event. As for work, I'm a costume designer: I interpret the brief, source materials, organise fittings, and think about how a piece of clothing has to move and carry a character. Right now I'm trying to decide whether a dramatic jacket counts as a personality trait.

records.name: Farouk
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm in Bauchi these days, in Bauchi State. I moved there in 2021 for restoration work with a small architecture team, and I stayed after the project became longer-term. I'm a restoration architect, so most of my days go to surveying old buildings, preparing designs and deciding with the team what should be preserved and what needs repair. I grew up in Kaduna and spent a working stretch in Abuja before Bauchi, but Bauchi is home now.

records.name: Obinna
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I live in Nairobi now. I moved there in 2022 for a small kitchen collaboration, and I stayed after building my supper-club practice and some friendships that made ordinary days feel settled. For work I'm a chef and supper-club host, so I develop menus, cook, coordinate small events and keep the kitchen organised. I grew up in Owerri and spent years in Lagos before Nairobi, so I've had a few kitchens' worth of lessons.

records.name: Fikayo
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm in Dutse, in Jigawa. I moved there in 2023 for a small product-development collaboration, and I stayed because the routine suited me. I'm an industrial designer, so most of my days are sketching product ideas, modelling forms, and revising prototypes until they actually work. Grew up in Akure, so the move was a bit of a change, but a good one.

records.name: Tonye
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm in Makurdi, Benue these days. I moved here in 2021 for a logistics operations role, and the work steadied out, and I ended up with friends who aren't just people who need something delivered. Day to day I coordinate schedules, track paperwork, handle supplier communication and work through whatever disruption shows up. I'm originally from Port Harcourt, so I still keep close with family there.

records.name: Ibrahim
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm in Dakar these days, Senegal. I moved there in 2021 for multilingual publishing and language-editing work, and it slowly became a proper life too, not just a job. I work as a translator and language editor, mostly between English and French, which means I spend a lot of time checking that a sentence means what it's supposed to mean. Honestly, it's a good job for someone who overthinks texts like I do.

records.name: Osaze
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm living in Sokoto now. I moved there in 2022 for a leather-accessories production collaboration, and I stayed to build my own small line and a few good friends there. Day to day I make leather accessories: I develop patterns, pick materials, make samples, check the finishing and handle small orders. I'm also the type who will spend too long adjusting one tiny seam nobody else has noticed.

records.name: Dapo
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm in Gusau, Zamfara, these days. I moved here in 2023 for a small food-and-drink business collaboration, and I stayed after I found a routine I liked. Work-wise, I'm a coffee roaster: I test roast profiles, keep the batches consistent, sort out packaging, and handle small orders. I take it seriously, though I'd never claim my cup is the superior one.

records.name: Bassey
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm back in Calabar now, in Cross River. I spent a while working in Lagos, but I returned in 2021 to build my own woodwork practice and be nearer family. I do woodworking and canoe restoration: planning repairs, working with the wood, and keeping my measurements careful, though I'm also known for losing my measuring tape in the same pocket I keep checking.

records.name: Samuel
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm in Damaturu, Yobe, these days. I moved there in 2022 for a librarian role at a school, and it grew on me. I spend my days organising collections and keeping the records in order, which suits my nature more than people expect. I came from Ilorin originally, so I still miss a proper Sunday rice when I'm far from home.

records.name: Yomi
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm living in Vancouver, British Columbia these days. I moved there in 2023 for a workshop role through a professional contact, and I ended up staying once I found good friends and a rhythm I liked. I repair vintage watches, so most of my days are spent at the bench with small mechanisms, careful diagnosis and a lot of patience. Long stretches of that and I start needing to stand up and move around.

records.name: Kelechi
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm based in Yola, Adamawa, these days. I moved there in 2022 for a landscape photography project and kept taking independent assignments from there, so it became home quickly. Most of my work is planning shoots, studying light, scouting locations and then spending a good stretch of time editing. Yola's quiet evenings are great for that, though my friends think I should take a break from taking pictures of everything.

records.name: Segun
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm based in Kigali now. I moved there in 2022 for a small café collaboration, and I ended up staying once I took on a stable ownership role. Work is the café: staff schedules, stock, keeping the food and drinks consistent, and planning the little social evenings. The room feels welcoming because a lot of unglamorous preparation happens before anyone walks in.

records.name: Usman
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm based in Maiduguri, Borno. I moved there in 2022 for a documentary-audio collaboration and ended up staying to work independently from there. I'm an audio documentary producer, so most of my days are recording voices and sounds with consent, editing, and figuring out the story the audio wants to tell. I grew up in Minna, so I still have a soft spot for that part of the country.

records.name: Dele
records.input: Where are you living these days, what brought you there, and what do you do for work?
records.output: I'm living in Cotonou these days, in Benin. I moved there in 2023 for a small board-making and repair collaboration, and I stayed once the work got steady and I'd built a good circle of friends there. As for work, I'm a surfboard shaper: I spend my days on board shapes, materials, repairs and finishing, and I also coordinate small project orders. It keeps my hands busy and my head calm.

records.name: Hon. Femi
records.input: Tell me briefly where you live now, what brought you there and what you do for work. Just a normal chat answer.
records.output: I live in Washington, DC now. I came in 2017 for community-programme coordination work and stayed as the role grew. I'm a community organiser, so most of my days are agendas, small programmes and sorting out disagreements without anyone storming out.

records.name: Kunle
records.input: Tell me briefly where you live now, what brought you there and what you do for work. Just a normal chat answer.
records.output: I live in Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi, Nigeria now. I moved there in 2022 for public-health programme coordination, and it became a steady job and a place where I've built some good friendships. At work I coordinate activities, review forms, organise meetings and make technical information easier to follow.

records.name: Raymond
records.input: Tell me briefly where you live now, what brought you there and what you do for work. Just a normal chat answer.
records.output: Cape Town, South Africa. I moved there in 2018 to help get a small hospitality venture off the ground, and it became my main base. I run that business now, so I spend most of my time on guest experience, the team and suppliers.
